name: Average strategy: Airbnb business travel, good segmentation but hedged recommendation
scratchpadNotes: road warriors vs extended stay vs offsites. needs: wifi, desk, check-in, Concur billing. hotels win 1-night. host incentives?

messages.text: Airbnb is considering a big push into corporate business travel to compete with Marriott and Hilton. Should they, and how?
What does success look like for this, is it a revenue target, or more about filling weekday nights which are weaker for Airbnb? And over what timeframe?
Think three years. The main motivation is weekday occupancy and a more predictable revenue stream.

Got it. I'd split business travel into a few segments, because they're really different. There's the solo road warrior doing one or two nights for a client meeting, there's extended stays like relocations or a consultant on a three-month project, and there are team offsites where a group wants to be together. Each has different needs.
Go on. Where does Airbnb stand in each?

For the one-night traveler, hotels are hard to beat. They want instant check-in, consistent Wi-Fi, a desk, and they want the booking to show up in Concur automatically. Airbnb is inconsistent on all of that. For extended stays, Airbnb is better, you get a kitchen and space, and it's cheaper for long periods. For offsites, Airbnb is kind of unique, because hotels don't really have a big house with ten bedrooms and a shared living room.

Probably a work-certified badge for listings, with verified Wi-Fi speed and a real desk. Concur and Navan integration for billing. And maybe a dedicated offsite search with large homes. I'd also need hosts to opt in, so some kind of incentive like better ranking.
Wouldn't Marriott respond? They have corporate contracts and loyalty programs.
Yeah, they'd probably push their extended-stay brands harder. I don't have a great answer for that, but I think the offsite use case is hard for them to copy.
Okay. So should Airbnb go after this or not?

I think it depends. If they can get enough hosts to meet the work standard, it could be really big. I'd probably start with all three segments in a few cities and see which one takes off, then double down. The risk is quality, since one bad stay can lose a corporate account, so I'd look at reviews closely.
